Boot the image under QEMU/OVMF across the frozen acceptance matrix — nominal 1/2/4/8 CPUs, AP-failure, and reboot — and keep the serial evidence per scenario. A scenario that is not run is reported as not run, never as passing.

```day-atom
{"in":["bootable-image"],"out":["boot-evidence"],"next":["determinism-check"],"done":["boot-evidence"]}
```

Physical hardware boot deferred to a later roadmap goal, with the analysis recorded so it is not redone. Key constraints: the runtime drives COM1 at 0x3f8 via PIO so the board needs a real 16550; GitHub-hosted runners are VMs so CI participation needs a self-hosted runner and a rig; and most of the acceptance matrix does not survive the move, since hardware gives one CPU count and AP-failure injection has no hardware equivalent.

validate_transcript in test-qemu.py is standalone and hardware-agnostic, so the definition of a passing boot is already written for hardware; only the transport would change. The cheap first step is a manual dd to USB, one boot, capture serial, feed it to that function — before building any rig.
